main_text.p: 2. Pet.i.19.20.21. Habemus firmissimū sermonem propheticum: cui recte facitis quòd attendatis, uelut lucernæ splenden ti in obscuro loco, ufq; dum dies illuce-scat, & lucifer exoriatur in cordibus ue-stris: si illud primum noueritis, quòd nul la Prophetia Scripturæ, sit proprij impul-sus, τῆς ἰδίας ἐπιλύσεως [?]. Non enim uoluntate hominis allata est olim Prophetia, sed acti à Spiritu sancto locuti sunt sancti Dei homines. Vt nihil aliud de hoc dicto dicam, erit uestræ pietatis, precari, ut quo acti Spiritu, locuti sunt Prophetæ, eodem nos quoq; ducamur, & in eorum interpretatione uersemur.

Cæterum quæ'nam & quanta sit Prophetarum auctoritas, & qua religione in eorum monumentis, Spiritus sancti Commentariis de fide, caritate & spe, uersandum nobis sit, diuus Chrysost. Homilia 2. in caput 6. Iesaiae, hisce uerbis mihi uidetur exposuisse: Prophetarum ora, Dei sunt os. Tale uero os nihil dixerit obiter extraq; rem. Ne igitur nos obiter & aliud agentes audiamus. Addit idem Chrysostomus elegas simile. Etenim si hi qui fodiunt metalla, ne minima quidè frustula

page.notes: Marginal reference "2. Pet.i.19.20.21." stands at the head of the column and is transcribed as text, as it appears set in the column; it may be a displaced marginal note. The Greek phrase "τῆς ἰδίας ἐπιλύσεως" is uncertain and marked [?]. The superscript "2" after "Homilia" is transcribed as printed. The word "quæ'nam" is printed with an apostrophe-like break. The catchword "præte-" and the signature "a 2" sit at the foot; the catchword is kept with its printed hyphen. Several print forms are kept as printed (ufq;, quidè, elegas, Chrysost.).
